hints.title: Most Frequent Element Constraint
hints.text: Duplicate numbers can never be placed into the same strictly increasing sequence. The maximum frequency dictates the minimum number of sequences required.

hints.title: Capacity Requirement
hints.text: If the most frequent element appears max_freq times, we need at least max_freq sequences, and each must have at least k elements.

hints.title: Necessary and Sufficient Condition
hints.text: Since the array is sorted, the condition len(nums) >= max_freq * k is both necessary and sufficient.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying to explicitly build the subsequence partitions is complex and unnecessary when checking feasibility.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting consecutive duplicates in sorted nums yields max frequency in linear time and O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize the pigeonhole frequency bottleneck and derive the inequality len(nums) >= max_freq * k.
complexity.notes: Consecutive equal elements count can be tracked in a single pass without extra structures.
